newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas slightly stronger on weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas slightly stronger on weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were slightly stronger on the day in Wednesday trade as western Canada braced for colder weather later in the week.
However, prices were off sharply from last week, when blizzards hit much of the U.S. Midwest, pushing up gas demand.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub was talked at C$2.70/2.75 per gigajoule, up about a dime from Tuesday, but well below last week's C$3.44 per GJ. Gas for February delivery fell to C$2.85 per GJ from C$3 on January 15.
Traders said they expected a gradual price rise over the next few days as the mercury dropped.

Environment Canada said temperatures in southern Alberta were forecast to drop to -20 Celsius (-4 Fahrenheit) amid high winds and blowing snow later Wednesday in a cold snap expected to last through the weekend.
"The extra demand from cold weather puts this market into overdrive," said a Calgary-based marketer, who predicted AECO gas in the C$2.85 per gigajoule range on Thursday.

He said the recent weakness in prices was partly because of scheduled maintenance on the TransCanada PipeLines Ltd system in northwestern Ontario, which was backing between 90 million and 175 million cubic feet per day into Alberta. The work was slated to continue through January.
At the borders, prices at Sumas, Wash. were talked in a wide range between US$2.38 and US$2.50 per million British thermal units with most deals in the upper part of the range.
The prices, although down about US$1.50 on the week, were about a dime higher than on Tuesday, as the western parts of north America were forecast to experience a cooling trend, traders said.
